record.title: Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5 processed raw NMR and LC-MS files for one contract-lab sample
record.summary: Anthropic’s Aug 18, 2026 technical report describes Claude Opus 5 using Claude Science to analyze raw NMR and LC-MS files from one routine contract-research-organization quality-control sample. Anthropic reports separate analyses completed in 23 and 19 minutes and compares them with that laboratory’s own processing and records. The report details a self-correction in its NMR interpretation and file-integrity checks for 2,664 mass-spectrometer scans. The headline purity figures use different peak sets: Anthropic reports 96.4% for three peaks, while the CRO report gives 96.33% for seven; the technical report calculates 98.8% from Claude’s own areas on the CRO’s peak basis. This is a detailed first-party account of one sample, not independent replication or evidence of general chemistry automation, therapeutic discovery, or broad productivity impact.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic published an Aug 18, 2026 account and a linked technical report describing Claude Opus 5 analysis of raw NMR and LC-MS files from one routine CRO quality-control sample.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic reports that two separate Claude Science sessions returned NMR and LC-MS analyses in 23 and 19 minutes, respectively, and that the output matched the CRO’s processing on the reported measurements.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic reports NMR peak agreement within 0.08 H for matchable peaks, a self-correction after its built-in audit found an overstatement, and exact reconstruction of stored ion totals for all 2,664 scans. These are first-party report results, not independent reproductions.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The report states that its headline 96.4% purity figure covers three detected peaks including the void peak, whereas the CRO’s 96.33% uses seven peaks; it reports 98.8% when Claude’s own areas are evaluated on the CRO’s seven-peak basis.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Independent accuracy, reproducibility on other samples or instruments, broad chemistry automation, general time savings, therapeutic discovery, and operational productivity effects are not established.

evidence_gaps.description: Public access to the raw FID and vendor LC-MS file, CRO audit trail and complete output is not established, preventing independent recomputation of the bounded case.
No independent group has rerun the workflow on this or another matched sample in this activation.
One sample does not quantify repeatable labor, turnaround, cost, error rates or workflow impact across a CRO or chemistry program.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported one-sample workflow is reproducible, it is a meaningful example of a general-access reasoning model handling raw analytical-chemistry instrument files with less specialist processing time. Its narrow single-sample scope and lack of independent or operational measurements keep consequence moderate.
limitations: The evidence is a detailed first-party account of one sample; the CRO comparison is reproduced within Anthropic’s report, not independently audited here.
The raw instrument files and CRO audit trail were not accessible in the reviewed public surface, so the reported processing and metrics could not be independently recomputed.
The 96.4% and 96.33% purity figures use different peak sets; they should not be presented as a direct agreement. The report’s 98.8% recalculation is also first-party.
No independent replication, multi-sample evaluation, time-and-motion study, cost analysis, safety assessment, therapeutic discovery, or broader operational impact is established.
brief.summary: Anthropic’s Aug 18, 2026 technical report describes Claude Opus 5 using Claude Science to analyze raw NMR and LC-MS files from one routine contract-research-organization quality-control sample. Anthropic reports separate analyses completed in 23 and 19 minutes and compares them with that laboratory’s own processing and records. technical.claimed_result: Anthropic reports 23-minute NMR and 19-minute LC-MS analyses, NMR peak agreement within 0.08 H where matched, and exact reconstruction of vendor-stored ion totals across 2,664 scans. Its own report distinguishes the 96.4% three-peak figure from the CRO’s 96.33% seven-peak result and reports 98.8% using Claude’s areas on the CRO basis.
technical.demonstrated_result: Anthropic’s publication and technical report exist and document the method and one sample. No execution or technical outcome was independently demonstrated in this review.
technical.mechanism: Claude Science coordinated two concurrent, separate sessions: one processed the CRO’s NMR free-induction-decay files and follow-up D2O spectrum; the other decoded a proprietary LC-MS binary file, extracted chromatography/mass/UV data, and compared its output with the CRO report. The technical report describes the model-side analysis workflow; it does not establish a general reusable chemistry pipeline.
technical.regime: One routine small-molecule CRO QC sample acquired July 31, 2026. Claude Opus 5 in Claude Science received raw proprietary NMR and LC-MS files and short prompts in separate parallel sessions. The report gives 400 MHz NMR and single-quadrupole LC-MS with PDA; no multi-sample or cross-instrument regime was evaluated.
technical.reproducibility: The report is accessible, but raw FID/LCD files and CRO audit trail were not found in the reviewed public surface, and no independent rerun was performed. The vendor-format validation checks are reported by Anthropic.
technical.strongest_baseline: The CRO’s own processing and audit trail for the same sample. This is a first-party comparison described by Anthropic; it is not an independent baseline audit or a matched study of many samples.

brief.title: Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5 processed raw NMR and LC-MS files for one contract-lab sample
brief.why_it_matters: Raw instrument-file interpretation can be a recurring, expertise-intensive step in experimental research. If the reported workflow generalizes, it could shorten analysis turnaround and make specialist processing more accessible. This case concerns one routine sample and an interested-party report; independent accuracy, reproducibility, time saved in operational use, and scale effects remain unestablished.
